presentingComplaint: Reduced urine output and lethargy for 3 days
history: Three-day history of markedly reduced urine output, generalised fatigue and nausea. Preceded by one week of profuse watery diarrhoea and poor oral intake with clinical dehydration. Background of type 2 diabetes and hypertension; regular medications include lisinopril and ibuprofen taken for recent back pain. No haematuria, frothy urine, rash or joint symptoms. No recent contrast imaging.
examination: Dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor and postural dizziness consistent with volume depletion. No peripheral oedema, no rash, no flank mass; bladder not palpable and no palpable distended bladder to suggest obstruction. Chest clear, no raised JVP.

labs.urinalysis: no blood, no significant protein; bland sediment with hyaline casts

imaging: Renal ultrasound: normal-sized kidneys, no hydronephrosis, no obstruction; bladder empty post-void
differentialDiagnoses: Pre-renal AKI from volume depletion (ACEi + NSAID + diarrhoea)
finalDiagnosis: Acute kidney injury (KDIGO stage 2, pre-renal/volume-depletion aetiology)
citations: KDIGO Clinical Practice Guideline for Acute Kidney Injury 2012
contraindications: Hold ACE inhibitor (lisinopril) and NSAID (ibuprofen) — nephrotoxic in volume depletion
Avoid iodinated contrast until renal function recovers
Dose-adjust or avoid renally-cleared drugs given reduced clearance
edgeCases: Prolonged pre-renal insult can transition to intrinsic acute tubular necrosis (FeNa >2%, muddy-brown granular casts)
Bland urinalysis argues against glomerulonephritis; active sediment/proteinuria would prompt an intrinsic-renal workup
expectedMaiK: Classic pre-renal AKI: an acute creatinine rise with oliguria in a volume-depleted patient on an ACE inhibitor plus NSAID after diarrhoeal losses. Withhold nephrotoxins, restore intravascular volume, treat hyperkalaemia and monitor for progression to ATN.
expectedNextQuestions: Any recent contrast exposure or new nephrotoxic drugs?
Baseline renal function and true urine output trend?
expectedInvestigations: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine electrolytes (FeNa/FeUrea)
Renal tract ultrasound to exclude obstruction
Serum potassium and ECG; venous blood gas for acidosis
